claims.text: The trip record and the trace describe the same trip and put the route well past the POL-RD-01 gate. The trace records 23.97 km driven against a booked optimal of 18.0 km — an excess of 5.97 km, or 33.17% of optimal. That clears both establishment tests: it is greater than 20% of optimal (3.6 km) and greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms. A route deviation is ESTABLISHED.

POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement, and it is 23.97 km; the trip record's rounded 24.0 km is a convenience copy of the same measurement and may NOT be cited for the threshold test. Here the point is academic because the two figures differ by 30 m and both clear every gate, so the finding is safe whichever field a reader picks up — but the ruling should rest on the trace figure, as the clause directs.

The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes. It carries 241 fixes at a 10 s sample interval over 100% coverage, with zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0 s, so none of POL-RD-07(a), (b) or (c) is engaged. The deviation therefore stands on the gps_trace alone and requires no independent corroboration of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) lists.

The driver's congestion story cites no artifact, and none exists to cite. EV-ADVIS-00114-01 is MISSING: its payload is null, its admissibility status is MISSING and its weight_multiplier is 0.0, with the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT recorded — no LTA advisory covers the AYE, the PIE or the Alexandra corridor in the 18:36–19:20 window on 7 August 2026. POL-RD-03 exoneration therefore fails at its first requirement: there is no advisory to name a road or expressway segment, no validity window, and no shortest_lawful_alternative_km from which the 130% cap could be computed. The absence of the artifact is itself citable, and it is relied on here only as an absence.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged on the documents. Limb (a): trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00114, with the trip record's started_at of 18:40:00 matching the trace's first_fix_at of 18:40:00 and its ended_at of 19:20:00 matching the trace's last_fix_at. Limb (b): the excess of 5.97 km meets the POL-RD-01 threshold and is measured from an unimpaired trace. The burden then shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause, and he points to neither — POL-RD-08 provides that a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's burden.

The driver's congestion excuse is a bare assertion that cites no evidence ID, and POL-RD-08 directs that such assertions be discarded — not escalated. POL-RD-10(5) fires where an exculpatory clause is invoked against a cited artifact that is missing from the pool. No clause is invoked here and no artifact is cited: the driver's own statement concedes 'No advisory that I know of', and his chat reply is no more than 'AYE jam boss, this way faster'. Reading a bare traffic excuse as a clause invocation would convert every uncorroborated excuse into an escalation and empty POL-RD-08's discard rule of content. The evidence the rider relies on is complete and every artifact that carries the deciding facts sits at weight 1.0, so no POL-RD-10 trigger is engaged.

No rider-requested detour. The chat log carries two messages and neither is an instruction: the rider's message asks 'adam road?? jurong is the other way', which is a challenge to the route, and the driver's reply gives no waypoint at all. POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction identifying a place or road specifically enough to act on, corroborated by travel the trace can verify; waypoint_hint is null on both messages and no road is named by the rider, so the clause is unavailable and nothing is excluded from the excess.

The remaining alternative and exculpatory clauses do not apply on this record. POL-RD-05 cannot be run: pickup_amended_at, dropoff_amended_at, amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are all null, so there is no amended endpoint and no re-quote to apply. POL-RD-12 does not apply: vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null. POL-RD-11 does not displace the arithmetic: fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so this is not an upfront-quoted trip and the distance-and-time refund is not closed off. POL-RD-02 governs the recomputation.

The POL-RD-02 recomputation runs as follows. Charged total 58.10. Recomputed fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 × 18.0 optimal km + 0.28 × 30.0 optimal min) × 1.6 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.50 of on-optimal-route ERP + 0.00 waiting fee − 0.00 promo = 41.12 + 0.80 + 2.50 = 44.42. Refund = 58.10 − 44.42 = 13.68, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 13.70. That is 23.5% of the charge: comfortably above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and far below the 90% line, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND.

The surge multiplier is taken from the artifact that carries it — fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier is 1.6 — and applied to base, distance and time only, never to the 4.50 of ERP. The rider does not contest the surge, and it is carried into the recomputed fare exactly as POL-RD-02 directs; the refund above is therefore the conservative figure, not one that quietly strips the multiplier out.

Of the 4.50 of ERP charged, the 2.50 Kim Keat Link gantry lies on the optimal route and is properly chargeable, while the 2.00 Adam Road gantry is off-route. Under POL-RD-09(1) that 2.00 off-route charge is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund, because the recomputed fare includes only on-optimal-route gantries; it is itemised for transparency and must NOT be added on top of 13.70. Neither charge is a phantom line: the trace passes within 250 m of both billed gantries, so POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity is not engaged on this trip.

No repeat-deviation uplift is claimed, and none is available. The excess of 5.97 km and 33.2% is below both materiality limbs (8.0 km absolute and 50% of optimal), so this is not a MATERIAL deviation and the POL-RD-06 consultation is not triggered. Even were the driver_profile consulted, the pattern test fails on its own terms: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 412, which is neither 3 or more flags nor a ratio of 0.05 or more. The correct remedy is the POL-RD-02 partial of 13.70, not a FULL_REFUND uplift and not a conduct referral.

The dispute is filed_by RIDER, so read against the filing party a PARTIAL_REFUND is a rider win: it returns 13.70 of the contested 15.00 to the rider and leaves the rider carrying only the optimal-route fare — base, the 18.0 km distance charge and 30 minutes of time at the metered rate, the surge the rider has accepted, the 0.80 platform fee and the 2.50 gantry the optimal route actually crosses. The rider's case that the extra 6 km and the off-route gantry are not his to pay is supported on this record.

claims.text: The deviation is established but it is not MATERIAL, and that distinction controls the remedy. The trace records 23.97 km against an 18.0 km platform optimal — an excess of 5.97 km, or 33.17%. That clears POL-RD-01's two establishment gates (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km), but it falls short of both materiality gates, which require more than 50% of optimal or more than 8.0 km absolute. The deviation is therefore ESTABLISHED and not MATERIAL, so the POL-RD-06 driver_profile consequences are not engaged by this trip.

No repeat-deviation pattern is established, so there is no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral. On the only fields POL-RD-06 permits, the driver's trailing-90-day record is deviation_flags_90d = 1 and completed_trips_90d = 412 — a flag count below the threshold of 3, and a ratio of 1/412 = 0.0024, an order of magnitude below the 0.05 test. POL-GEN-01 confines this test to exactly those two fields, and both fall short.

The ceiling on any rider recovery is the POL-RD-02 arithmetic, not the 15.00 the rider asserts. The fare_model is METERED, so: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 18.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x 1.6) + 0.80 + 2.50 = 41.12 + 0.80 + 2.50 = 44.42; charged_total = 58.10; refund = 58.10 - 44.42 = 13.68, rounded up to 13.70. That is 1.30 below the amount contested, and the rider's figure is overstated by that much.

The ERP must not be counted twice, and the rider's reliance on '4.50 of ERP' overstates the correction. Of the 4.50 charged, only the 2.00 Adam Rd gantry is off the optimal route (on_optimal_route false); the 2.50 Kim Keat Link gantry lies on it (on_optimal_route true, and it is the figure carried as optimal_route_erp_sgd). Under POL-RD-09(1) the off-route 2.00 is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 recomputation and must never be added on top of it, while the on-route 2.50 is a properly chargeable pass-through that stays with the rider.

No billing-integrity correction is available to the rider. The trace has 100% coverage with no gaps, and it passes within 250 m of both billed gantries, so neither line is a phantom crossing under POL-RD-09(4) and neither is refundable as a standalone correction.

The driver does not claim exoneration under POL-RD-03, and says so plainly rather than stretching the record. That clause requires a traffic_advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses with a validity window overlapping the passage, and EV-ADVIS-00114-01 is MISSING — status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — with no LTA advisory covering the AYE, the PIE or the Alexandra corridor in the 18:36-19:20 window. The driver's congestion account in the counterparty statement is honest but unsupported by the artifact the clause requires, so the clause cannot be run and no advisory-based exoneration is asserted.

The chat log neither shifts any excess to the rider nor grounds driver compensation. The only rider message is a query sent at 18:58:40, minutes after the vehicle had left the optimal corridor: 'adam road?? jurong is the other way'. It carries no waypoint_hint and gives no instruction to take a particular road, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable and its corroboration test cannot be run on this record. The compensation limb likewise fails: billed distance (24.0 km) exceeds the trace figure (23.97 km), so there is no unbilled shortfall above 1.0 km and nothing to compensate.

In the alternative, the very gap that defeats the driver's exoneration is an escalation trigger in its own right. POL-RD-10(5) makes escalation mandatory where an exculpatory clause is asserted with no supporting artifact in the pool — its own example being 'a closure asserted with no traffic_advisory'. That is this case: the driver asserts an external traffic cause under POL-RD-03, and the required advisory is absent from the pool, EV-ADVIS-00114-01 carrying the MISSING_ARTIFACT issue at weight 0.0. On that reading the disputed amount should be held for a human reviewer rather than refunded on a record that cannot answer the traffic question either way.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver — this ruling is for both of you.

WHAT HAPPENED. The trace for TRP-00114 records 23.97 km driven against a booked optimal of 18.0 km: an excess of 5.97 km, or 33.17% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass (more than 20% of optimal and more than 0.8 km absolute). The excess does not reach either materiality gate (more than 50% of optimal, or more than 8.0 km), so this is an established but not a MATERIAL deviation, and the POL-RD-06 driver-profile consequences are not triggered. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing figure; the trip record's 24.0 km is a rounded copy of the same measurement and was not used for the threshold. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes — 241 fixes, 10 s interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0 s — so none of POL-RD-07(a)–(c) fires and the deviation stands on the trace alone. (The admissibility pre-pass also left this artifact COMPLETE, so schema status and policy status agree here.)

THE DRIVER'S CONGESTION ACCOUNT. The driver's statement that the AYE was crawling and no advisory was known is an assertion that cites no evidence ID, and POL-RD-08 provides that a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, carries no weight and is discarded. It also cannot discharge the driver's shifted burden, and it does not exonerate: POL-RD-03 requires a traffic_advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses with an overlapping validity window, and EV-ADVIS-00114-01 is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT) — no LTA advisory covers the AYE, PIE or Alexandra corridor in the 18:36–19:20 window. The driver's alternative escalation argument under POL-RD-10(5) is rejected: that limb fires where an exculpatory clause is invoked against a cited artifact that is absent from the pool. Here no clause is invoked against any artifact — the congestion claim is a bare assertion citing nothing, and the driver's own primary position is that no POL-RD-03 exoneration is asserted. POL-RD-08's discard rule, not escalation, is what governs a bare excuse; otherwise every uncorroborated excuse would become an escalation. The absence of the advisory is citable, but the ruling does not rest on that artifact, so it does not touch the confidence floor.

NO OTHER EXONERATION. POL-RD-04 fails: the rider's message 'adam road?? jurong is the other way' is a challenge to the route, not an instruction, it carries no waypoint_hint and names no road the driver could act on. POL-RD-05 fails: no amendment timestamps and no amended optimal are stored, so there is nothing to re-run and POL-RD-05 cannot be applied (its own terms send a null re-quote to POL-RD-10(5), which is not the case here since no amendment is recorded at all). POL-RD-12 fails: vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null. POL-RD-11 fails: fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so the distance-and-time refund is not closed off.

THE MONEY. POL-RD-02 runs on the metered fare, with the surge multiplier taken from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier = 1.6 and applied to base, distance and time only, never to ERP.
